newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Wednesday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover rose to 1.7 billion yuan from 1.594 billion on Tuesday and the 90-day contract was again the most active.
Traders said talk that the central bank would not cut bank interest rates this year supported the rates.
There was talk that Dai Xianglong, the governor of the People's Bank of China, had denied indirectly the rumour of a further cut in bank interest rates this year.
This gave the market a little support and prevented the rates from edging down in the short term, traders said.
"The day's weak performance of domestic A shares prevented some non-banking financial institutions from buying actively," one trader said. "But the new issues on Thursday will support the rates."
Local traders expected the rates to move in a narrow range in the next few days.
